title: Write and read a small file
summary: printf writes text. A redirection sign sends that text into a file. cat prints a file's contents.
introduction: printf writes text. A redirection sign sends that text into a file. cat prints a file's contents. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain write and read a small file
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: printf writes text. A redirection sign sends that text into a file. cat prints a file's contents.

blocks.title: Write and read a small file

blocks.text: The file contains two lines: Moon and Ocean. The single > creates or replaces the named file.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Use a different new file name and write three lines.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A single > overwrites existing contents. Use it only on a practice file you intend to replace.
For more detail later, use this [Linux further reading](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html).
